players.name: LuciaBot
players.description: Always removes an entire row: the first one that is not empty.

players.name: ManuelBotUsopp
players.description: Perfect nim-sum player: always leaves the XOR of the rows at zero. From a lost position it removes as little as possible, leaving the opponent the fewest winning replies so any slip can be punished.

players.name: NimSumBot
players.description: It would always win if possible using XOR rule.

players.name: XorMaster
players.description: Plays the nim-sum strategy: always moves to a position whose XOR is zero. When already losing, it stalls by taking one stick from the largest row to give the opponent more chances to err.

players.name: easy
players.description: Always empties the largest row. A plausible-looking rule that is barely better than random: taking as much as possible just hands the opponent a simpler position.

players.name: hard
players.description: Minimax with alpha-beta pruning, searching 4 plies. Recognises several endgames outright — a single row, all-ones boards by parity, mirrored rows, and a few tabulated positions — and steers play toward the endgames it knows. Strong, but it cannot see every losing position.

players.name: medium
players.description: Minimax with alpha-beta pruning, searching 2 plies and then guessing from the number of sticks left. Solid right at the end of a game, unreliable before that.

players.name: random
players.description: Picks uniformly at random among all legal moves. No strategy at all — the baseline every other player has to beat.
